title: Cloud Shell, the editor and the ephemeral machine that comes with it

videos.script: Open a terminal in the console, and Google starts a small machine for you. That is Cloud Shell. {{machine}} gcloud, Terraform and Docker are already there. So are your credentials. It costs nothing. {{free}} It is a machine in Google's project, not yours. So it is not in your network, and it cannot reach your private addresses. {{network}} Each session gets a fresh machine. Your home directory comes back. Everything else does not. {{home}} A script in your home called customize environment runs as root at every start. That is how a missing package is always there. {{customize}} There is an editor, and a web preview that only you can open. {{editor}} And there are limits: hours a week, the length of a session, the size of the home. {{limits}} Two things to decide before you rely on it. It acts as you, with every role you hold. And an administrator can switch it off. So write runbooks that need only a terminal with gcloud. {{end}}
